·         Conflict is a process, where perception (real or otherwise) leads to disruption of desirable state of harmony.

·         Types of conflicts:

o   Conflicts may be intrapersonal (conflict with self), interpersonal (between two persons) and organizational.

o   Organizational conflict is again classified into interorganizational (conflict between 2 groups) and intraorganizational (intragroup) conflicts.

o   Intragroup conflict (or infighting) refers to conflict between two or more members of the same group or team.

·         Manifest is not a type of conflict. In fact, it is one of the five stages of conflict.

1.      Latest stage: people may be in conflict without being aware that they are in conflict

2.      Perceived stage: people involved in a conflict become fully aware that there is a conflict

3.      Felt stage: stress and anxiety are felt by one or more of the participants due to the conflict

4.      Manifest stage: the conflict can be observed in this stage

5.      Aftermath stage: takes place when there is some outcome of the conflict

·         Among and Between are the prepositions that are always confusing among the English users.

·         Among is used in reference to the association of more than two entities when they are a part of group and Between is used in reference to the association of two or more distinct individual items.

·         Examples:

o   Between—“The match is between India and Australia. (Here in the sentence there is association between 2.)

o   Plural noun or pronoun comes with between. E.g.: Argument between the students. Here in the sentence between is used before the plural noun students.

o   Among: Captain distributed sweets among the players. (Here in the sentence there is association of more than 2)

o   In and Into: We generally use in, when we talk about the position when something is in relation to a larger area around, and into, when we talk about the movement of something in a direction or towards a destination.

·         Examples:

o   In—Geeta is in a room. (sentence shows where the Geeta is)

o   Into—Geeta is entering into the room. (Sentence shows Geeta is going inside the room).

The uterus bulges or slips into the vagina, sometimes so far that it comes out of the vaginal opening.

The rectum bulges into or out of the vagina.

The small intestine bulges against the back wall of the vagina. An enterocele and vaginal vault prolapse often occur together.

choices.correct_explanation:
·         ‘No, not me’ reaction of the patient is seen in denial stage of impending death (Terminal Patients). The Kubler Ross stages of grief in terminal illness are popularly known by the acronym DABDA.

      

Table: Kubler Ross stages of grief

Stage

Explanation

 Denial

In this stage, individuals believe the diagnosis is somehow

mistaken, and cling to a false, preferable reality. Example- No, this can’t happen to me.

 

Anger

When the individual recognizes that denial cannot continue, they become frustrated, especially at proximate individuals. Example- How can this happen to me?

 

Bargaining 

The third stage involves the hope that the individual can avoid a cause of grief. Usually,

the negotiation for an extended life is made in exchange for a reformed lifestyle. People facing less serious trauma can bargain or seek compromise.

Examples include the terminally ill person who negotiates with God to attend a daughter’s marriage.

 

Depression

During the fourth stage, the individual despairs at the recognition of his mortality. In this state, the individual may become silent, refuses visitors and spends much of the time in mournful and sullen state

 

Acceptance

 

In this last stage, individuals embrace mortality or inevitable future, or that of a loved one, or another tragic event. People dying may precede the survivors in this state, which typically comes with a calm, retrospective view for the individual, and a stable condition of emotions.

choices.title: Lag phase
choices.correct_explanation:
• The lag phase is the initial phase of bacterial growth where the bacteria adjusts to their new environment. During this phase, there is little to no increase in the number of bacterial cells as they are synthesizing new components necessary for growth. It's a period of adaptation before the bacteria enter the exponential growth phase.

·         The stationary phase is the phase of bacterial growth where the population size remains relatively constant. This occurs when the rate of cell division equals the rate of cell death. Nutrient depletion, waste accumulation, and other environmental factors contribute to the cessation of exponential growth.

·         The phase of decline, also known as the death phase, occurs after the stationary phase when the number of viable cells begins to decrease. This decline can be due to nutrient depletion, buildup of toxic waste products, or other unfavorable conditions that lead to cell death.

·         The logarithmic phase, also called the exponential phase or log phase, is characterized by rapid cell division and exponential increase in the number of bacterial cells. During this phase, bacteria are actively multiplying, and the population size doubles at regular intervals. It follows the lag phase and precedes the stationary phase.

  •  In summary, option (d) is the correct answer as it describes the phase characterized by exponential growth in bacterial population. Options (a), (b), and (c) describe other phases of bacterial growth.

choices.correct_explanation:
·         The most common preventable complication of abdominal surgery is Atelectasis. Minor lung collapse may occur as postoperative complications of abdominal surgeries.

·         Atelectasis refers to a partial collapse of the small airways. The majority of post-operative patients will develop some degree of atelectasis, resulting in abnormal alterations in lung function or compromise to the lung’s immune defense.

·         The pathophysiology of atelectasis is not fully understood. However, current theories suggest that airway collapse is due to a combination of airway compression, alveolar gas resorption intra-operatively and impairment of surfactant production. General anesthesia is another common cause of atelectasis.

·         It changes the regular pattern of breathing and affects the exchange of lung gases, which can cause the air sacs (alveoli) to deflate.

·         Postoperative atelectasis can be asymptomatic, or it may manifest as increased work of breathing and hypoxemia. The most effective treatment for atelectasis is deep breathing exercises and chest physiotherapy. This ensures that the airways are opened maximally and coughing can be performed effectively.

·         The other preventable complications are fluid and electrolyte imbalance (prevented by intravenous fluid administration, blood transfusion), followed by urinary retention (prevented by treating the cause, intravenous fluid and drug administration), and lastly thrombophlebitis (prevented by proper IV site care, early ambulation, blood thinners administration, etc.).

choices.correct_explanation:
·            During performance appraisal there are several errors that take place by supervisor; one of them is Halo effect.

·            Halo effect:  When a single positive or negative dimension of a subordinate’s performance is allowed to influence the supervisor’s rating of that subordinate on other dimensions, a halo effect is operating. For example:  the supervisor likes Tom because he is very cooperative. 

·            Horn effects: It is a type of cognitive bias where a person’s impression of another can substantially influence one’s thoughts and feelings about that person. Other errors are strictness or leniency, and recency of event. 

·            Paired comparison: It is a method of appraisal where one employee is compared with all other employees in a group for only one trait/small range of options at a time.

·            Paired comparison and horns effects are not the error of performance appraisal.

·            Central tendency error: Some raters are reluctant to rate subordinates as very high or very low. They dislike being too strict with anyone by giving them an extremely low rating, and they may believe that no one ever deserves to get the highest possible rating.

·         From: Preposition from shows the separation or removal from something or somewhere.

·         With: Preposition with shows together, involved, having, using, etc.
